title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document codifies Redwood Inference SRE standards for SLO definition and measurement, error budget policy and enforcement, capacity planning cadence and guardrails, reliability initiative lifecycle, incident review standards, recommended operational tooling, and canonical runbook templates. It is intended for engineers, on-call SREs, and product owners responsible for production SLAs.

Key Principles
- Measure what matters: SLOs should reflect user-visible outcomes (latency, availability, correctness) rather than internal metrics only.
- Make error budgets actionable: define clear thresholds and automated/operational responses for budget burn.
- Plan capacity conservatively for 95th-99th percentile workloads and validate with load tests and canaries.
- Prioritize reliability work through a transparent initiative pipeline tied to SLO impact.
- Post-incident learning > blame; convert reviews into actionable changes and experiments.

1) SLOs and Error Budgets
- SLO format: <Objective>: <Target> over <Window>. Examples: 
  - API availability: 99.95% successful requests per calendar month (hosted inference endpoint /v1/generate).
  - Tail latency: P99 latency < 500ms for small prompt path (<= 128 tokens) measured over 30 days.
  - Embedding correctness: top-k precision >= 92% on canonical benchmark set over 30 days.

- SLO measurement sources: Prometheus metrics (service:request_success_total, service:request_latency_seconds_bucket), gateway logs, application traces (Tempo), and synthetic canaries. All SLO queries must be stored in the central SLO repo (slo-queries/).

- Error budget policy (monthly window):
  - Green: budget remaining > 30% - normal rollout and reliability work proceeds.
  - Watch: budget remaining between 10% and 30% - pause low-risk releases that increase capacity utilization; require an owner sign-off for risky rollouts.
  - Restrict: budget remaining <= 10% - freeze feature rollouts that affect the service, prioritize mitigations and reliability fixes, require approval from SRE lead.
  - Exhausted: budget hit - initiate emergency reliability sprint (see "Reliability Initiative" section) and notify stakeholders.

- Automated actions: PagerDuty runbook triggers when budget crosses watch/restrict thresholds; automated throttling rules at the gateway for non-critical traffic when restrict is hit.

2) Capacity Planning
- Cadence: Quarterly formal capacity planning with monthly refreshes for critical services.
- Inputs: historical QPS, 95th/99th percentile CPU/GPU utilization, tail latency, KV-cache hit rates, model size/version mix, commit/rollout plans, expected marketing events.
- Safety margins: target headroom = max(20% of steady-state capacity, 2x expected traffic variance). For Dedicated pools allow configurable burst capacity of 20-40% depending on SLA tier.

- Process (quarterly):
  1. Collect telemetry snapshots and forecast demand for next quarter.
  2. Run supply-side simulation using the capacity planning tool (infra/capacity-sim).
  3. Validate with targeted load tests (canary namespace) and update autoscaler policies.
  4. Publish capacity plan and required procurement requests.

- Key metrics to track (monthly):
  - Provisioned GPUs/VMs, average and peak GPU util%, request concurrency, queue depth, P99 latency, inference errors per 100k, cache hit rate.

3) Reliability Initiatives (RIs)
- RI definition: cross-functional projects aimed to materially improve SLO attainment or lower long-term cost of reliability.
- Prioritization criteria: SLO impact, incident frequency, operational cost, customer visibility, complexity and ROI.
- Lifecycle: Proposal -> Triage (SRE + Product) -> Charter (owner, success metrics, timeline) -> Implementation -> Verification (A/B canary + metric guardrails) -> Close & Share learnings.

Example RI charters: model warm-starting to reduce P99 generation latency by 30%; KV cache multi-region replication to increase availability for region failover.

4) Incident Review Standards
- Trigger: any Sev-1/Sev-2 incident or when SLO breach occurs.
- Timeline: postmortem draft within 72 hours; final review within 10 business days.
- Postmortem template (required fields):
  - Summary (executive one-liner)
  - Impact (customers, services, SLOs)
  - Timeline (annotated)
  - Root cause analysis (5 Whys / contributing factors)
  - Immediate mitigations and long-term fixes (owners + ETA)
  - Action items (tracked in backlog with priority)
  - Lessons learned and verification plan

- Review board: SRE lead, service owner, product manager, and one cross-functional engineer. Action items must be tagged as reliability initiatives or runbook updates.

5) Operational Tooling and Observability
- Recommended stack:
  - Metrics: Prometheus + Thanos for long-term retention.
  - Dashboards: Grafana (per-service dashboards + SLO dashboards).
  - Tracing: OpenTelemetry + Tempo (distributed traces tied to SLO failures).
  - Logs: Loki / ELK with structured logging (JSON).
  - Alerting: Alertmanager with on-call routing to PagerDuty.
  - Synthetic monitoring: k6 / gatling canaries run from multiple regions.

- Tooling ownership and baseline dashboards: each service must publish a canonical Grafana dashboard including request rate, error rate, P50/P95/P99 latency, resource utilization, and SLO burn graph. Dashboards should include annotated runbook links and playbook buttons.

- CI/CD safety hooks: pre-rollout integration tests for load and regression, and automatic rollback on canary SLO regressions.

6) SRE Runbook Templates
- Purpose: actionable, step-by-step guides for common and high-impact incidents. All runbooks live in confluence under eng-sre/runbooks and as executable playbooks in the runbook repo (playbooks/).

- Canonical runbook structure (flat fields):
  - Title
  - Scope and symptoms
  - Impact classification
  - Owner and escalation path
  - Detection queries and dashboard links
  - Immediate mitigation steps (1-3) with CLI/console commands
  - Triage checklist
  - Post-incident tasks

- Example: Inference-serving high tail latency (P99 > 750ms)
  1. Confirm detection: check service:request_latency_seconds_bucket, Grafana P99 panel.
  2. Check recent deploys: `git log -n 5 --pretty=oneline` and CI/CD rollout status.
  3. Verify model variant and quantization profile in use.
  4. If capacity-related: scale up dedicated pool (CLI example):
     - `ri infra scale pool inference-gpu-pool --count +2 --reason "auto-runbook: p99 latency spike"`
  5. If queue buildup: drain non-critical background traffic by flipping feature flag `feature.disable-low-priority-requests`.
  6. If memory pressure: restart node with leak mitigation label: `k rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n prod --labels leak-mitigation=true`.
  7. Engage perf owner to capture flamegraphs and heap checks (link to profiling playbook).

7) Governance and Compliance
- SLO ownership: every production service must have a documented SLO owner (team and individual) and a published SLO page.
- Quarterly SLO review: SRE leads and product managers review SLO definitions and adjust windows/targets if product or usage changes materially.
- Document retention: incident postmortems and action items retained for 3 years.

8) Templates and Artifacts
- Required artifacts for new services: SLO definition, canonical dashboard, capacity plan snapshot, runbook for top 3 failure modes.
- Sample SLO query (Prometheus):
  `sum(rate(service_request_success_total{job="inference-api"}[30d])) / sum(rate(service_request_total{job="inference-api"}[30d]))`

9) Contacts and Ownership
- SRE Oncall Rotation: see eng-sre/oncall (link). Primary contact: oncall@redwood.ai.
- SRE leads: Ari Chen (past), Priya Singh (availability), Lucas Martin (capacity).

Appendix A - Quick checklists
- Pre-Release checklist: SLO impact assessment, canary plan, capacity headroom verification, rollback plan.
- Incident triage checklist: detect, contain, stabilize, mitigate, restore, postmortem.

Appendix B - Example KPIs
- Monthly: SLO attainment %, number of Sev1 incidents, mean time to recovery (MTTR), % of action items closed within SLA.

Notes and next steps
- Action: All service owners should ensure SLO pages and runbooks are current within 30 days of this publication.
- Feedback: Send comments to eng-sre@redwood.ai or add reviewer in page metadata.

End of document
